relevance_note: Three individually described males with LAMP2 deletions: "We analyzed three males with clinical and pathological findings consistent with Danon disease".
method_note: Read the full text by hand and built the JSON with a short Python script (values typed from my reading; no table transcription, the paper has no tables). Labels Case-1/Case-2/Case-3 follow the text's most frequent form; the paper also uses subject IDs 0014, 00732 and 0013. Relatives of Case-2 ('the available family members', 'normal family samples', a 'control individual from the family of Case-2') were tested by Southern blot and western blot and were negative, but the paper never says how many or who they are (only a pedigree in Figure 3D), so no rows were created for them rather than inventing people. Inheritance for Case-2 left 'not reported': the paper calls the deletion de novo but names only 'available family members', not both parents, as tested; the statement is in parental_testing_statement. Contradiction: the Abstract gives Case-2 a 64kb and Case-3 a 58Kb deletion, but the Figure 3C legend calls Case-2's (00732) the '∼58kb microdeletion'; breakpoints in Results are ∼14kb/∼72kb (Case-2) and ∼14kb/∼78kb (Case-3). Deletion sizes were therefore not put in the Case-2/Case-3 variant strings. No HGVS c./p./g. descriptions are printed; breakpoints are given only relative to the start codon, so genomic_coordinates_as_stated is null. Transcript ENST00000371345 is printed in the Case-1 and Case-2 molecular sections; the Methods' general reference NM_013995 was not assigned to any person, and Case-3 transcript left 'not reported'. Variant type 'large deletion/CNV' comes from the statement naming the three individuals as carrying 'large genomic deletions'. Zygosity left 'not reported' (all male, but no per-person statement). Pathogenicity left 'not reported': the authors say Danon disease is 'caused by microdeletions' but give no classification term. Case-1 pre-excitation is described as 'possible'; checklist pre-excitation marked observed on the basis of the stated short PR interval. Case-3 has 'no evidence of skeletal muscle weakness' but biopsy 'myopathy': weakness excluded as a feature row, while the composite checklist item 'proximal muscle weakness (skeletal myopathy)' is marked observed from the biopsy myopathy. Case-2 age at onset left 'not reported' (only age at first presentation, 12, recorded as onset of GI problems); age at Danon diagnosis not stated explicitly. Case-2 age at death not stated (two months after the MRI at 21), so deceased_age is null.
